title: Fresh medium versus high reasoning screen
hypothesis: Medium reasoning reduces coding latency on task families excluded from its original screen while retaining correction context, environmental recovery and verified correctness.
falsified_if: Medium loses correctness or request activation, or fails the preregistered latency/cost gates.
local_evidence: Historical medium reasoning was 21.89% faster in the initial screen but was never validated on reserved task families. Low reasoning failed held-out speed validation. This independent current-engine medium screen follows the prompt screen chronologically but uses the unchanged current prompt in BOTH arms regardless of its result.

task_suffixes.simple_prompt: This task is self-contained; do not browse or use external network services.

deterministic_outcomes: independently graded artifacts, protected scope and completed verification
actual request model, effort, prompt and tool activation
decision_rule: Seed 922. Six screen-only launches, one per arm on simple_prompt and two coding tasks. Simple control first, coding order and adjacent arm order randomized. Maximum $1.75 between-run standard-equivalent cost threshold (one-run overshoot possible), 360 active worker seconds. No retries. Stop on correctness, protocol or activation failure; retain all resource accounting. Advance only if all six pass, aggregate coding latency is at least 10% lower, neither coding task is more than 10% slower, and aggregate coding cost rises no more than 10%. Otherwise park this implementation pending a materially new hypothesis. Simple runs are excluded from coding effects but included in spend. A positive screen justifies fresh replication only, never a default change. Preserve current source and fixtures, audit actual requests, run grader positive/negative preflight and verify activation before continuing.
